FOUNDATIONAL INCORPORATION
What the U.S. considers uniquely "American" -the cowboy,
the western ranch, the capitalist expansion- was built directly
upon centuries-old Spanish and Mexican blueprints.
Mexican economic models, labor structures, and cultural
adaptations are not alien to the United States; they are the
bedrock of its continental power.

The Ecological Borderlands
The Navajo Sheep Empire:
Adopted Spanish Churro sheep to
transition into powerful pastoralists,
dominating the San Juan Basin.
The Comanche Horse Empire:
Harnessed the Spanish horse to
become nomadic bison-hunting
warriors, controlling the Great Plains
and dictating terms of trade.
Native societies absorbed the European ecological
invasion and transformed it into geopolitical power.

> Borderland Blueprints
Mexico is not an alien counterpart to the United
States; it is its foundational architect.
From 16th-century silver mining to 21st-century
labor flows, the economic dynamism of the
United States rests permanently upon
Hispanic blueprints.
To understand the future of North America, we
must stop defending an artificial dividing line,
and finally recognize the shared
foundation beneath it.
